## Sign In Endpoint

This endpoint allows users to authenticate by signing in with their email and password. Upon successful authentication, the server responds with user details and an access token.

### Request

- **Method**: POST
    
- **URL**: `localhost:{{port}}/auth/sign-in`
    
- **Request Body** (JSON):
    
    - `email` (string): The email address of the user attempting to sign in.
        
    - `password` (string): The password associated with the user's account.
        

### Example Request Body

``` json
{
  "email": "seller2@gmail.com",
  "password": "Password123!"
}

 ```

### Response

- **Status**: 200 OK
    
- **Content-Type**: application/json
    
- **Response Body** (JSON):
    
    - `user`: An object containing user details.
        
        - `banned` (boolean): Indicates if the user is banned.
            
        - `_id` (string): The unique identifier for the user.
            
        - `name` (string): The user's name.
            
        - `surname` (string): The user's surname.
            
        - `age` (integer): The user's age.
            
        - `email` (string): The user's email.
            
        - `phone` (string): The user's phone number.
            
        - `password` (string): The user's password (not typically returned).
            
        - `roleId` (string): The role identifier for the user.
            
        - `accountType` (string): The type of account the user has.
            
        - `deleted` (boolean): Indicates if the user account is deleted.
            
        - `isVerified` (boolean): Indicates if the user's email is verified.
            
        - `createdAt` (string): Timestamp of when the user was created.
            
        - `updatedAt` (string): Timestamp of the last update to the user.
            
    - `token`: An object containing authentication tokens.
        
        - `access_token` (string): The token used for accessing protected resources.
            
        - `refresh_token` (string): The token used to obtain a new access token.
            

### Request

- **Method**: POST
    
- **URL**: `localhost:{{port}}/auth/sign-in`
    
- **Headers**:
    
    - `Content-Type: application/json`
        

#### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and include the following parameters:

- `email` (string): The email address of the user attempting to sign in.
    
- `password` (string): The password associated with the user's account.
    

**Example Request Body**:

``` json
{
  "email": "seller2@gmail.com",
  "password": "Password123!"
}

 ```

### Response

Upon a successful sign-in, the server will return a response with a status code of `200` and the following JSON structure:

- `user` (object): Contains information about the authenticated user.
    
    - `banned` (boolean): Indicates if the user is banned.
        
    - `_id` (string): The unique identifier for the user.
        
    - `name` (string): The user's first name.
        
    - `surname` (string): The user's surname.
        
    - `age` (integer): The user's age.
        
    - `email` (string): The user's email address.
        
    - `phone` (string): The user's phone number.
        
    - `password` (string): The user's password.
        
    - `roleId` (string): The role identifier associated with the user.
        
    - `accountType` (string): The type of account the user has.
        
    - `deleted` (boolean): Indicates if the user's account is deleted.
        
    - `isVerified` (boolean): Indicates if the user's email is verified.
        
    - `createdAt` (string): The timestamp when the user was created.
        
    - `updatedAt` (string): The timestamp when the user was last updated.
        
- `token` (object): Contains the authentication tokens.
    
    - `access_token` (string): The token used for accessing protected resources.
        
    - `refresh_token` (string): The token used to obtain a new access token.
        

**Example Response**:

``` json
{
  "user": {
    "banned": true,
    "_id": "",
    "name": "",
    "surname": "",
    "age": 0,
    "email": "",
    "phone": "",
    "password": "",
    "roleId": "",
    "accountType": "",
    "deleted": true,
    "isVerified": true,
    "createdAt": "",
    "updatedAt": ""
  },
  "token": {
    "access_token": "",
    "refresh_token": ""
  }
}

 ```

# Get My Car Ads

This endpoint retrieves a list of car advertisements associated with the authenticated user.

## Endpoint

```
GET /carAds/myAds

 ```

## Method

`GET`

## Expected Input Parameters

This endpoint does not require any input parameters in the request.

## Response Format

The response will be in JSON format and will include the following fields:

- `ads`: An array of car advertisement objects, each containing details about the ad.
    
    - `id`: Unique identifier for the advertisement.
        
    - `title`: Title of the car advertisement.
        
    - `description`: Description of the car being advertised.
        
    - `price`: Price of the car.
        
    - `createdAt`: Timestamp of when the ad was created.
        
    - `updatedAt`: Timestamp of when the ad was last updated.
        

### Example Response

``` json
{
  "ads": [
    {
      "id": "1",
      "title": "2018 Toyota Camry",
      "description": "A well-maintained sedan with low mileage.",
      "price": 20000,
      "createdAt": "2023-01-01T12:00:00Z",
      "updatedAt": "2023-01-10T12:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "2",
      "title": "2019 Honda Accord",
      "description": "A reliable car with excellent fuel efficiency.",
      "price": 22000,
      "createdAt": "2023-02-01T12:00:00Z",
      "updatedAt": "2023-02-10T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

## Notes

- Ensure that the user is authenticated to access their ads.
    
- The response will return an empty array if no ads are found for the user.
    

This endpoint retrieves a list of car advertisements that belong to the authenticated user. It allows users to view their own ads, including details such as the car's make, model, price, and other relevant information.

### Request

- **Method:** GET
    
- **URL:** `localhost:{{port}}/carAds/myAds`
    

### Response

The response will be in JSON format and will include an array of car ads. Each car ad object may contain the following fields:

- `id`: (string) Unique identifier for the car ad.
    
- `make`: (string) The manufacturer of the car.
    
- `model`: (string) The model of the car.
    
- `year`: (integer) The year the car was manufactured.
    
- `price`: (number) The price of the car.
    
- `description`: (string) A detailed description of the car.
    
- `imageUrl`: (string) URL to an image of the car.
    

### Example Response Structure

``` json
{
  "ads": [
    {
      "id": "12345",
      "make": "Toyota",
      "model": "Camry",
      "year": 2020,
      "price": 20000,
      "description": "A reliable sedan with great fuel efficiency.",
      "imageUrl": "http://example.com/images/car1.jpg"
    },
    {
      "id": "67890",
      "make": "Honda",
      "model": "Civic",
      "year": 2019,
      "price": 18000,
      "description": "Sporty compact car with advanced safety features.",
      "imageUrl": "http://example.com/images/car2.jpg"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

### Notes

- Ensure that the user is authenticated to access this endpoint.
    
- The response will only include ads that are created by the authenticated user.
